# Elements in a small yard do not display what they should

### What happens
`recording.mp4` (0:32) shows a small yard: two floating elements hang side by side, and a penguin
walks a loop in front of them, carrying a smaller floating element above its head. Seen from the
front, all three floating elements display the same thing. From about 0:15 the camera walks around
the left floating element and then looks at the yard from behind. At several moments of the clip,
the floating elements and the penguin do not display what they should. These are separate,
independent defects, each affecting a different case; fixing one does not fix the others. The
terrain, the hills and the sky are drawn correctly.

### Expected
Each of these elements displays exactly what it was set up to display, at every moment and from
every side it is seen from. This must hold for any such element anywhere in the world and however it
is placed, turned or carried, not only for the elements and camera positions shown in the video.

### Environment
All.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect any moment of the video by pulling frames out of it with `ffmpeg` (installed in the
image). Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it
does not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

language = "C++"
framework = "Luanti (Minetest)"
cross_file = true
visual_essentiality = "required"
difficulty = "hard"

The video is the only place the five independent defects can be seen, all of them in the client's sprite-entity rendering (the "sprite" and "upright_sprite" visuals), spread over three source files plus the bundled Irrlicht engine. None of them logs anything, leaves a compiler warning, or breaks an existing unit test; the entity state the server and Lua see is correct in every case, so only the rendered pixels show them:

1. Left board frozen on "A" (the original issue #15105, src/client/content_cao.cpp + mesh.cpp/.h): the upright_sprite's frame is applied by rewriting the texture coordinates of a mesh whose vertices live in a static GPU buffer, and the buffer is never marked dirty, so the GPU keeps the first frame forever. 2. Camera-facing sprites mirrored (irr/src/CBillboardSceneNode.cpp, constructor): the billboard's corner texture coordinates are assigned with U flipped, so every "sprite" entity is drawn mirrored. In the video the right board's B, C and D read backwards and the penguin's side views point the wrong way, so it moonwalks when it crosses the yard. The defect sits in the engine library, not in Luanti's own sprite code, which looks correct.
3. Back of upright boards mirrored (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::addToScene): the back quad of an upright_sprite reuses the front quad's corners with the winding reversed, which reads naturally but maps the texture mirrored when seen from behind. From 0:23 the left board's back shows a mirrored "E" (its back sheet is E-F-G-K). The front is unaffected.
4. Penguin shows the wrong side (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::updateTexturePos): select_x_by_camera adds the entity's yaw to the camera bearing instead of subtracting it. Subjects turned along the view axis are unaffected; turned across it, front and back swap (seen along Z) or left and right swap (seen along X). In the video the penguin shows its back while walking towards the camera and its face while walking away.
5. Carried board frozen on "A" (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::step): the sprite frame timer was moved into the "not attached" branch of the movement code, so a sprite attached to another object never advances its animation. The board above the penguin's head stays on "A" while the two big boards cycle. It is a billboard, so fixing defect 1 does not touch it.

Several defects interact in the video (the penguin's moonwalk comes from defect 2, its back/face swap from defect 4, and the frozen carried board looks like defect 1 but has a different cause), so a fix guided only by one symptom is easy to get wrong: swapping the left/right or front/back columns of select_x_by_camera makes the penguin look right in this camera direction but fails the probes seen along the other axis, and flipping only the board that looks wrong leaves the other sprite paths broken.

The hidden tests run the real client headlessly (Xvfb, Mesa llvmpipe) on the devtest game with a probe world mod and classify the dominant colour of fixed screen regions over time (the whole scenario is run a second time if the harness itself fails, e.g. a client crash). Animated probes (an upright_sprite, an attached sprite, an attached upright_sprite, and an upright_sprite whose frame the mod changes with set_sprite() every second) must keep cycling through the sheet's frames in order at about one frame per second, and the animated ones must show the same frame as an identical unattached camera-facing sprite started at the same moment most of the time. A camera-facing sprite and the back of an upright_sprite with a four-quadrant texture must show each texture corner in the matching screen corner (catches mirrored and upside-down fixes). Four select_x_by_camera sprites turned to 0/90/180/270 degrees, seen once along -Z and once along +X, must each show the documented column for the side facing the camera. f2p per defect: 1 -> upright_sprite_animates, upright_sprite_follows_set_sprite, attached_upright_sprite_animates; 2 -> sprite_texture_is_not_mirrored; 3 -> upright_sprite_back_is_not_mirrored; 4 -> camera_facing_sprite_shows_the_side_facing_the_camera; 5 -> attached_sprite_animates, attached_upright_sprite_animates.   "src/client/content_cao.cpp",
  "src/client/mesh.cpp",
  "src/client/mesh.h",
]
f2p = [
  "sprite_probe upright_sprite_animates",
  "sprite_probe upright_sprite_follows_set_sprite",
  "sprite_probe sprite_texture_is_not_mirrored",
  "sprite_probe upright_sprite_back_is_not_mirrored",
  "sprite_probe camera_facing_sprite_shows_the_side_facing_the_camera",
  "sprite_probe attached_sprite_animates",
  "sprite_probe attached_upright_sprite_animates",
]

  "sprite_probe reference_sprite_animates",
  "sprite_probe upright_sprite_renders_a_palette_color",
  "sprite_probe reference_sprite_renders_a_palette_color",
  "sprite_probe upright_sprite_front_is_not_mirrored",
]

# Elements in a small yard do not display what they should

### What happens
`recording.mp4` (0:32) shows a small yard: two floating elements hang side by side, and a penguin
walks a loop in front of them, carrying a smaller floating element above its head. Seen from the
front, all three floating elements display the same thing. From about 0:15 the camera walks around
the left floating element and then looks at the yard from behind. At several moments of the clip,
the floating elements and the penguin do not display what they should. These are separate,
independent defects, each affecting a different case; fixing one does not fix the others. The
terrain, the hills and the sky are drawn correctly.

### Expected
Each of these elements displays exactly what it was set up to display, at every moment and from
every side it is seen from. This must hold for any such element anywhere in the world and however it
is placed, turned or carried, not only for the elements and camera positions shown in the video.

All.

You can inspect any moment of the video by pulling frames out of it with `ffmpeg` (installed in the

The video is the only place the five independent defects can be seen, all of them in the client's sprite-entity rendering (the "sprite" and "upright_sprite" visuals), spread over three source files plus the bundled Irrlicht engine. None of them logs anything, leaves a compiler warning, or breaks an existing unit test; the entity state the server and Lua see is correct in every case, so only the rendered pixels show them:

1. Left board frozen on "A" (the original issue #15105, src/client/content_cao.cpp + mesh.cpp/.h): the upright_sprite's frame is applied by rewriting the texture coordinates of a mesh whose vertices live in a static GPU buffer, and the buffer is never marked dirty, so the GPU keeps the first frame forever. The camera-facing board next to it (a billboard drawn from client memory) animates.
2. Camera-facing sprites mirrored (irr/src/CBillboardSceneNode.cpp, constructor): the billboard's corner texture coordinates are assigned with U flipped, so every "sprite" entity is drawn mirrored. In the video the right board's B, C and D read backwards and the penguin's side views point the wrong way, so it moonwalks when it crosses the yard. The defect sits in the engine library, not in Luanti's own sprite code, which looks correct.
3. Back of upright boards mirrored (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::addToScene): the back quad of an upright_sprite reuses the front quad's corners with the winding reversed, which reads naturally but maps the texture mirrored when seen from behind. From 0:23 the left board's back shows a mirrored "E" (its back sheet is E-F-G-K). The front is unaffected.
4. Penguin shows the wrong side (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::updateTexturePos): select_x_by_camera adds the entity's yaw to the camera bearing instead of subtracting it. Subjects turned along the view axis are unaffected; turned across it, front and back swap (seen along Z) or left and right swap (seen along X). In the video the penguin shows its back while walking towards the camera and its face while walking away.
5. Carried board frozen on "A" (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::step): the sprite frame timer was moved into the "not attached" branch of the movement code, so a sprite attached to another object never advances its animation. The board above the penguin's head stays on "A" while the two big boards cycle. It is a billboard, so fixing defect 1 does not touch it.

I found and fixed three separate rendering bugs. The client builds, and test renders under a virtual display show the fixed behaviour.

**1. Every `sprite` entity was drawn mirrored left-to-right** (the right-hand element, and the small one the penguin carries). In `irr/src/CBillboardSceneNode.cpp`, the billboard's texture coordinates were flipped relative to its corners: the bottom-right corner was given the left edge of the texture. That's why B, C and D in the video show up mirrored, and why the corner dot on the "A" sprites sits on the opposite side from the one on the left element. I swapped the coordinates so each corner gets the matching part of the image.

**2. The back face of an upright sprite showed its texture mirrored** (the green "E" seen from behind the left element). In `src/client/content_cao.cpp`, the back face reused the front face's corner positions with the winding reversed, so its texture came out flipped. Now the back face's corners are mirrored, so its texture reads the right way round. Animated upright sprites still pick the right frame on both faces after this change.

**3. The penguin always faced the wrong way.** The penguin is a sprite sheet that picks a front, side or back image depending on the viewing angle. The code that picks the image added the entity's yaw (heading) where it should subtract it (`float dir = mob_dir - m_rotation.Y;`). That gave the right image only at yaw 0, which is why the penguin seemed to walk backwards wherever it went. Subtracting gives the right image for any heading and any camera position. It also uses the same yaw direction as the engine's built-in "face the direction of movement" option.

**How I checked it:** I built a small throwaway world (in `/tmp`, outside the repo) with three test entities: a sprite, a two-sided upright sprite, and a six-column yaw sprite. Each image had a marker in its top-left corner, and I took screenshots under Xvfb:
- From the front and from behind, every marker appeared top-left and each side of the upright sprite showed its own texture.
- From both sides, the yaw sprite showed the expected sheet column. Turning it by 90° moved to the column you'd expect.

The unit tests weren't run because this binary was built without unit-test support.

Only those two files changed, and nothing is committed.
